text.p: Swedish mining and rubber group Trelleborg said on Tuesday that its Trelleborg Industri unit has bought the North American company Yale-South Haven Inc that has an annual turnover of about one billion crowns ($134.9 million).
Trelleborg Industri is responsible for the company's rubber operations.
Trelleborg said Yale-South Haven, based in South Haven, Michigan, had an annual turnover of one billion crowns and 900 employees with five factories in the U.S. and Mexico.
Its main product is anti-vibration components for cars and some of its largest customers are General Motors, Chrysler and Ford.
"The acquisition is a link in our aspiration to be one of the leading players in the world in vibration-dampening components for the car industry," said Trelleborg's managing director Kjell Nilsson.
He said by combining resources in Trelleborg Automotive, the companies would meet the vehicle industry's demand for increased services from subcontractors.
Nilsson said Trelleborg Industri and Yale-South Haven had since 1994 worked closely in Europe and North America.
No financial details on the deal were given.
-- Belinda Goldsmith, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1045 ($ = 7.413 Swedish Crowns)
